description: k3s-lab on the shared preset github>KevinDeBenedetti/renovate-config: Monday-morning schedule, 3-day soak, labels, github-workflows pins left to its propagate-release job. Renovate replaced Dependabot, which bumped the actions only, on 2026-11-23: it also moves the upstream subcharts with the copies of their versions in the chart READMEs, the Vault image of platform-vault, the Ansible collections, the Helm CLI and the Python linters of the workflows, and the prek hooks. semanticCommits is forced on rather than detected: the commit type decides what release-please releases.

customManagers.description: Subchart versions restated in the Subchart(s) row of each chart's README, written `name` [`version`](repository) like the Chart.yaml dependency they copy. Same name and repository, so the copy moves in the PR of the Chart.yaml. Not platform-traefik's: disabled below.

The Vault image tag platform-vault's README restates twice (its `Vault image` row and its values table): moved in the vault PR with the values.yaml pin. The row still said 1.21.2 after the pin moved to 1.21.4 on 2026-08-06.
Python tools pinned as 'name==version' in the `pip install` of a workflow (ansible-core and ansible-lint in the ansible job of ci.yml): no manager reads a run step.

packageRules.description: The third-party actions in one PR, as Dependabot's `actions` group did: one CI run and one review instead of one per action. A major still gets a PR of its own (separateMajorMinor).

The Helm CLI of setup-helm, every `version:` of the workflows in one PR. CI lints and renders the charts with it, but release-charts.yml also logs in to GHCR, packages and pushes them with it, on main only, after the merge: no PR runs those commands.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ release-charts.yml runs `helm registry login`, `helm package` and `helm push` with this Helm, on main only: no pull request exercises them. Read this major's notes on those commands before merging, and watch the next Release Charts run.

packageRules.description: The platform-* pins of the umbrella (charts/platform-deployment) are release-please's: an extra-file of its config, moved in its release PR and guarded by check-umbrella-pins.sh. Renovate must never propose them.

What charts/ holds is what a published chart deploys: its upstream subcharts (Renovate rewrites the Chart.lock next to the Chart.yaml in the same PR; the kyverno-policies CI job reads the kyverno version from it), the images its values pin, the README copies of their versions. `fix(deps)`, so release-please lists the bump under Bug Fixes and proposes the release that publishes it.

A major of a subchart or of an image can break the values or the resources of the chart that wraps it, for whoever installs that chart: the reviewer decides, and marks the commit breaking when it does (commit-types: `!` bumps the minor while on 0.x).
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ A major. If it changes the values or the resources this chart renders for its users, merge it as `fix(deps)!: …`, so release-please records a breaking change and bumps the minor.

packageRules.description: Lock file maintenance (config:best-practices, weekly) rewrites Chart.lock files only, and opens nothing when just their `generated:` line would change: the pins are exact. release-charts.yml regenerates each Chart.lock before packaging anyway, so no published chart changes: `chore(deps)`, no release.

No digest on the images of charts/ (the Vault server of platform-vault, and the README copies of its tag): check-rendered-images.sh compares what follows the last ':' of the rendered image with the pinned tag, so `tag: "1.21.4@sha256:…"` would fail it.
The vault subchart and the Vault image platform-vault pins in one PR: the image overrides the appVersion of that same subchart.

kube-prometheus-stack ships a major almost every month, most of them for a prometheus-operator CRD update: one PR to its latest major, not the preset's one per major, which proposed seven at once from 86.x (dry run, 2026-11-23).

platform-traefik's README states, next to the subchart version, facts of that subchart Renovate cannot know (the proxy it deploys, the annotations of its Chart.yaml), and check-traefik-image.sh verifies them together: those copies stay verified, not generated. A human writes the page in the traefik PR.
What CI refuses in a traefik PR until a human does it.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ CI fails until `charts/platform-traefik/README.md` agrees with this subchart. Run `./scripts/check-traefik-image.sh` and update what it reports: the `| Subchart |` row, the `| Deployed proxy |` row (the new subchart's appVersion) and the annotation block under `# charts/traefik/Chart.yaml (subchart …)`, with the prose that cites them. Check the advisory table, then push that commit to this branch.

packageRules.description: The `>=` floors of ansible/galaxy.yml are what the collection asks of its consumers: raised on purpose, never to each new release. requirements.yml holds the exact versions CI installs.

The collections of ansible/requirements.yml: CI and local runs install them, the published collection does not ship the file (build_ignore), hence the default `chore(deps)`. CI's syntax-check resolves every module, so a major that drops one the roles call fails the PR.
The pip pins of the workflows are CI tooling: `ci(deps)`, like the actions.
ansible-lint supports only some ansible-core releases: both in one PR, so CI never runs an unsupported pair.
